question.:question/problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1\text{st},$ $3\text{rd},$ and $4\text{th}$ rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & -9 & 7 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 & -8 \\ 0 & -5 & 1 & -6\end{bmatrix}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1\text{st},$ $3\text{rd},$ and $4\text{th}$ rows of $A$ are $8,$ $4,$ and $-5$, respectively.

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & -9 & 7 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 & -8 \\ 0 & -5 & 1 & -6\end{bmatrix}
$$

So, the answer is $8+4+(-5)=7.$

question.:question/problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1\text{st},$ $2\text{nd},$ and $4\text{th}$ rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 3 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & -6 & -4 \\ -6 & 2 & -6 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{bmatrix}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1\text{st},$ $2\text{nd},$ and $4\text{th}$ rows of $A$ are $3,$ $-1,$ and $-3$, respectively.

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 3 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & -6 & -4 \\ -6 & 2 & -6 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{bmatrix}
$$

So, the answer is $3+(-1)+(-3)=-1.$
